Kitchen Equipment and Exhaust Are Easy to Underestimate — ₹2.5 lakh to ₹30 lakh+ depending on format, often quoted separately from the interior fit-out.

contentHtml:
Restaurant interiors in India typically cost from about ₹500 per sq ft for a basic budget fit-out to ₹1,500 to ₹6,000 per sq ft for designed café and restaurant interiors in Delhi NCR. Kitchen equipment, furniture, air-conditioning, licences and rent deposits are usually extra. Total startup budgets range from about ₹5 to ₹20 lakh for a café to ₹40 lakh to ₹1.5 crore for fine dining.

Ask five people what a restaurant interior costs and you will get five answers, because a ₹5 lakh café fit-out and a ₹1 crore fine-dining room are both "restaurant interiors". The honest answer depends on the format, the size, the condition of the space and how much of the kitchen, air-conditioning and bar you are building. This guide breaks down restaurant interior design cost in India by format, line by line, so you can build a budget that survives the site.

Key numbers at a glance

ItemTypical range
Interior fit-out, budgetFrom about ₹500 per sq ft
Interior fit-out, designed café or restaurant (Delhi NCR)About ₹1,500 to ₹6,000 per sq ft
Kitchen equipment, café to medium restaurantAbout ₹2.5 lakh to ₹18 lakh
Licences (excluding liquor)About ₹1 to ₹2 lakh
Liquor licenceAbout ₹2 to ₹8 lakh a year, varying by state
Security deposit on leaseCommonly 6 to 12 months' rent
Premium Gurgaon rent (e.g. Cyber City)Above ₹300 per sq ft per month

Restaurant cost by format

The format decides the size, the kitchen and the level of finish, and therefore most of the budget.

FormatTypical sizeTotal startup investmentKitchen equipment
Cloud kitchen200 to 400 sq ft (kitchen only)₹5 to 15 lakh₹2 to 6 lakh
Café or coffee shop300 to 1,000 sq ft₹5 to 20 lakh₹2.5 to 7 lakh
QSR or fast food300 to 800 sq ft₹10 to 25 lakh₹1.5 to 4 lakh (small takeaway)
Casual dining (about 30 seats)800 to 1,500 sq ft₹15 to 40 lakh₹3 to 8 lakh (₹8 to 15 lakh premium)
Bar, brewery or lounge1,500 to 4,000 sq ft₹30 to 80 lakhVaries by menu and bar
Fine dining (about 50 seats)2,000 to 5,000 sq ft₹40 lakh to ₹1.5 crore₹15 to 30 lakh+

Total startup figures include rent deposit, equipment, interiors, licences, working capital and initial inventory. They are national benchmarks; premium Gurgaon and Delhi locations sit at or above the top of each range.

How much of that is the interior?

The interior fit-out (civil work, flooring, ceilings, lighting, electrical, plumbing, joinery, bar counter, finishes and furniture) is the biggest controllable cost. Two useful reference points:

  • Budget fit-outs: one national guide puts a 30-seat casual dining interior at about ₹5 to 15 lakh for 800 to 1,200 sq ft, which works out to roughly ₹420 to ₹1,900 per sq ft.
  • Designed interiors in Delhi NCR: a Delhi NCR studio puts café interiors at about ₹1,500 to ₹6,000 per sq ft, with ₹1,200 per sq ft possible for a minimalist fit-out.

That gives a practical way to read any quote:

Interior tierIndicative rate per sq ftWhat it looks like
Basic₹500 to ₹1,500Existing shell reused, paint and lighting refresh, standard furniture
Designed₹1,500 to ₹3,500Full concept, custom bar or counter, feature ceiling, acoustic treatment, layered lighting
Premium₹3,500 to ₹6,000+Bespoke joinery, natural stone, imported fittings, detailed lighting and sound design

Where the money goes: a line-by-line breakdown

Use this as a checklist when comparing quotes. Every line below appears in a real restaurant budget, whether or not it appears in a designer's quote.

Cost headTypical figureNotes
Design and drawingsFee or % of projectConcept, 3D, working and licensing drawings
Civil work and partitionsSite dependentKitchen walls, washrooms, bar, levels
FlooringAbout ₹60 to ₹200 per sq ft installedTiles or vinyl in kitchens; stone or timber look front of house
False ceiling and lightingSite dependentLighting design is where the room's mood is made
Electrical and power upgradeAbout ₹80,000 to ₹3 lakhKitchen and air-conditioning loads often need a higher sanctioned load
Air-conditioningAbout ₹60,000 to ₹2 lakh (splits, ~800 sq ft); more for centralPlus ₹2 to 5 lakh if you choose central AC
Kitchen exhaust and ductingAbout ₹30,000 to ₹1.5 lakh+Large kitchens can run to several lakh
Kitchen equipment₹2.5 to ₹30 lakh+ by formatSee the format table
Furniture and tablewareAbout ₹2 to 5 lakh for 30 seatsDining chairs about ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 each
WashroomsSite dependentGuests judge your kitchen by them
Signage and façadeSite dependentNeeds a signage permit
LicencesAbout ₹1 to 2 lakh, plus liquor if applicableFSSAI, fire NOC, trade licence, music licence
Contingency10% of the fit-outFor what the survey could not see

What changes the cost most

  1. Condition of the space. A bare shell needs flooring, ceilings, washrooms and services from scratch. A previous restaurant site may have usable exhaust, drainage and power, and that can save lakhs.
  2. The kitchen and exhaust. Kitchen equipment, gas lines, ventilation and fire suppression form a large share of the budget, and the exhaust route often decides the layout.
  3. Air-conditioning and power. Restaurants run heavy loads. Upgrading the sanctioned electrical load and installing air-conditioning are among the most commonly missed costs.
  4. The bar. A full bar adds a counter, back bar, refrigeration, plumbing and the liquor licence.
  5. The finish level. Natural stone, custom joinery, imported lighting and acoustic treatment move a project from designed to premium.
  6. Location. Mall outlets have their own fit-out rules and timings; high-street and standalone sites need façades and signage.

Costs most first-time owners miss

  • GST on interiors, usually quoted separately.
  • Electrical load enhancement and the power backup it requires.
  • Fire suppression over the cooking line and fire alarms in the dining room.
  • The mall or landlord's fit-out deposit and approval charges.
  • Rent during the fit-out period, if it is not rent-free.
  • Pest control, grease traps and drainage work.
  • Reinstatement at the end of the lease.
  • Music and other recurring licences.

A worked example: 1,000 sq ft casual dining outlet in Gurgaon

Indicative only, using the ranges above:

ItemLowHigh
Interior fit-out (₹1,500 to ₹3,500 per sq ft, designed tier)₹15 lakh₹35 lakh
Kitchen equipment₹5 lakh₹8 lakh
Furniture and tableware₹2 lakh₹5 lakh
Air-conditioning, exhaust and power upgrade₹2 lakh₹6.5 lakh
Licences (excluding liquor)₹1 lakh₹2 lakh
Contingency (10% of fit-out)₹1.5 lakh₹3.5 lakh
Total before GST, rent and depositabout ₹26.5 lakhabout ₹60 lakh

Add the security deposit (commonly 6 to 12 months' rent) and working capital. At premium Gurgaon rents above ₹300 per sq ft per month, the deposit alone on 1,000 sq ft can exceed the interior budget.

Seven ways to control the budget without hurting the room

  1. Choose a site with usable services. Existing exhaust, drainage and power can save more than any finish change.
  2. Spend where diners look and sit. Lighting, seating, the bar and washrooms. Save on back-of-house finishes.
  3. Freeze the layout before execution. Changes after the kitchen and partitions are built are the most expensive kind.
  4. Plan licensing drawings with the design. Fire exits and kitchen layouts redrawn late cost time and money.
  5. Buy kitchen equipment to the menu. Used equipment can cut kitchen costs by 30 to 50%, though it needs checking.
  6. Use one itemised BOQ. It makes value engineering possible and prevents gaps between contractors.
  7. Keep a 10% contingency. Restaurant sites always hide something.

faqs.question: How much does restaurant interior design cost in India?
faqs.answer: Restaurant interiors in India range from about ₹500 per sq ft for a basic fit-out to ₹1,500 to ₹6,000 per sq ft for designed café and restaurant interiors in Delhi NCR. Kitchen equipment, furniture, air-conditioning and licences are usually extra.

faqs.question: What is the interior cost per sq ft for a café in Delhi NCR?
faqs.answer: Published Delhi NCR figures put café interiors at about ₹1,500 to ₹6,000 per sq ft, with around ₹1,200 per sq ft possible for a minimalist fit-out. The finish level, kitchen scope and site condition decide where a project falls.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to open a restaurant in India?
faqs.answer: Total startup costs typically range from about ₹5 to 20 lakh for a café, ₹10 to 25 lakh for a QSR, ₹15 to 40 lakh for a 30-seat casual dining outlet, ₹30 to 80 lakh for a bar or lounge, and ₹40 lakh to ₹1.5 crore for fine dining.

faqs.question: How much does commercial kitchen equipment cost in India?
faqs.answer: Roughly ₹2.5 to 7 lakh for a small café, ₹4 to 10 lakh for a small restaurant, ₹8 to 18 lakh for a medium restaurant and ₹15 to 30 lakh or more for large or fine-dining kitchens. Exhaust and gas work may be priced separately.

faqs.question: What hidden costs should I budget for in a restaurant fit-out?
faqs.answer: GST, electrical load enhancement, fire suppression and alarms, landlord or mall fit-out deposits, rent during the fit-out, grease traps and drainage, recurring licences and reinstatement at the end of the lease. Keep a 10% contingency.

faqs.question: Does the interior cost include kitchen equipment and furniture?
faqs.answer: Not always. Some designers quote the shell and finishes only; turnkey firms often include furniture but quote kitchen equipment separately. Ask for a written list of inclusions and exclusions before comparing quotes.

faqs.question: How can I reduce restaurant interior costs?
faqs.answer: Choose a site with usable exhaust, drainage and power, spend on what diners see and sit on, freeze the layout before execution, plan licensing drawings early, size kitchen equipment to the menu and work from one itemised BOQ.
